headline: Golden Knights activate Parker Wotherspoon off injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Golden Knights have activated defenseman Parker Wotherspoon off injured reserve. He had missed 13 games after an upper-body injury on October 10, and Jesse Granger of The Athletic posted a day earlier that he was on the ice at Vegas practice in a regular jersey.

Vegas (12-5-2) didn't stall without him, but his early numbers suggest he's a useful piece to get back. In his six games so far this season, VGK controlled 55.75% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) at five-on-five with him on the ice, against 52% for the team overall. The team's share of expected goals is also 3.21 percentage points better when he plays. He averages 18.26 minutes a game, so this is a real role, not a depth cameo. He has no points, but his own expected goals of 0.24 sit almost exactly on his zero goals, so there's no scoring bad luck to correct. This is a defender for his play without the puck, and as a fantasy option he offers little, with 30 points last season in 80 games for PIT as the ceiling. Six games is a small sample, so we'd treat the on-ice edge as encouraging, not settled.
